scenes.text: No warning. No trace. Just darkness.
The oceans go haywire. Tides collapse by two thirds.
Animals that steer by moonlight? Their compass is gone.
But here's the twist. After twenty four hours, almost nothing bad happens.
The real nightmare? If it never comes back.
The Moon is the anchor holding Earth's tilt steady.
Lose it, and over millions of years, our seasons could swing from freezing to scorching.
Now look up tonight. It's still there. For now.
